questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-{45}^{∘})=\frac{1}{2}
$$

  

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as

$$
x={15}^{∘}+{72}^{∘}\cdot n,\,x=b+{72}^{∘}\cdot n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $b$ in the range $[{0}^{∘},{72}^{∘}).$

$b=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-{45}^{∘} & ={30}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \, & \, & 5x-{45}^{∘} & ={150}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ={30}^{∘}+{45}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & 5x & ={150}^{∘}+{45}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ 5x & ={75}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & 5x & ={195}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ x & ={15}^{∘}+{72}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & x & ={39}^{∘}+{72}^{∘}\cdot n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $b={39}^{∘}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
$$

  

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi ,\,x=b\pi +2n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $b?$
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+2\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{2\pi }{3}+2\pi n \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $b=\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi }{8})=-\sqrt{3}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +2n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
questions.worked_solution:
The given equation is equivalent to 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi }{8})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$

So, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi }{8} & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{8}-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{2} & =-\frac{\pi }{24}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=-\frac{1}{12}.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the general solution of the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\sec\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \sqrt{2}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\cos\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
2x + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2\pi n, \qquad\qquad 2x + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{7\pi}{4} + 2\pi n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x=-\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n, & \, & \, & 2x=-\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{7\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ 2x=-\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n, & \, & \, & 2x=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ x=-\frac{\pi }{8}+\pi n, & \, & \, & x=\frac{5\pi }{8}+\pi n\end{aligned}
$$
